q1-im1-sets-pictures.alt: Four pictures of sets as circles: one holding a cat, a fork, a watermelon and a chair; one labelled all numbers; two overlapping circles; and two separate circles that do not touch.

q1-pr1-4x3-tiling.alt: A 4 by 3 board covered by six 2 by 1 dominoes: three horizontal dominoes stacked in the left half, one horizontal domino across the top row of the right half, and two vertical dominoes below it.

q1-ap-ordinate-2x2.alt: Graph of f(x) = 2x squared rising from the origin, with dotted vertical segments at x and at b marking the ordinates 2x squared and 2b squared.

q1-ap-ordinate-x3.alt: Graph of f(x) = x cubed rising from the origin, with dotted vertical segments at x and at b marking the ordinates x cubed and b cubed.

q1-ap-number-line.alt: A number line with arrows at both ends and tick marks labelled x, then dots, minus 1, 0, 1, dots, and y.

q1-ap-sup-max.alt: Two number lines. On the left, the closed interval S from 0 to 1 ends in a filled dot at 1 labelled max S, with the upper bounds hatched to its right. On the right, the interval T from 0 to 1 ends in an open dot at 1 labelled least upper bound or sup T, with the upper bounds hatched to its right.

q1-ap-venn.alt: Four diagrams of two sets A and B drawn as circles: overlapping circles with both shaded for the union; overlapping circles with only the overlap shaded for the intersection; two separate circles for disjoint sets, whose intersection is empty; and two separate shaded circles showing that a union can also look like this.

r1-work-hours-mapping.alt: Mapping diagram from work hours to pay: 25 to $500, 53 to $310, 30 to $490 and 40 to $490; a dashed arrow from 30 to $310 is crossed out, since one input may not have two outputs.

r1-difference-quotient.alt: Sketch for the difference quotient: a line through the points at heights f(x) and f(x+h) on the vertical axis, whose horizontal separation is h.

r1-vertical-line-test.alt: Vertical line test: (a) input and output axes with a vertical line at one input; (b) a line and (c) a parabola meet every vertical line once, so they are functions; (d) a sideways parabola, (e) a circle and (f) a vertical line meet some vertical line more than once, so they are non-functions.

r1-features-graph.alt: Graph of f on [-6,11] through (-6,-3), (-4,0), (-2,3), (0,5), (4,3), (6,0), (8,-3), (10,0) and (11,1); the line y=2 meets it at x=-3 and x=5, and the x-axis is shaded green where f is positive and blue where it is negative.

r1-domain-range-graphs.alt: Four graphs: (a) a sine-like curve on [-pi, pi] with outputs between -1 and 1; (b) an increasing exponential-type curve that stays above the x-axis; (c) a curve rising from the origin to an open circle at (4,5); (d) a curve rising from minus infinity near x=0 to an open circle at (7,12).

r1-even-odd-graphs.alt: Four graphs: (a) an even function on [-4,4], symmetric about the y-axis, with (-4,2), (-3,0), (0,3), (3,0), (4,2); (b) an odd cubic-like curve through (-2,-1), the origin and (2,1); (c) an exponential-type curve that is neither even nor odd; (d) the odd function 1/x through (-1,-1) and (1,1).

r1-incr-decr-graphs.alt: Four graphs with the x-axis marked into falling and rising stretches: (a) the even graph through (-4,2), (-3,0), (0,3), (3,0), (4,2); (b) the odd curve with turning points (-2,-1) and (2,1); (c) a curve with low points at x=-2 and x=2 and a high point at x=0; (d) a log-like curve that only rises.

r1-extrema-graphs-1.alt: Two graphs: (a) a closed curve from (-3,2) down to (-1,-1), up to (3,5) and down to (6,0); (b) a curve from the closed point (0,-3) up to an open circle at (3,5) and down to an open circle at (6,2).

r1-extrema-graphs-2.alt: Four graphs: (c) from (-4,5) down to (-1,2), up to (2,4), down to (5,1); (d) from (-2,2) down to (-1,1), up to (2,4), then falling without bound beside a dashed vertical line; (e) from (-4,3) down to (-2,0), up to (0,5), down to (3,1), then rising without bound beside a dashed vertical line; (f) a curve with closed endpoints whose low and high turning points, including (5,5), are open circles.

r1-avg-rate-of-change.alt: An increasing curve with the points (a, f(a)) and (b, f(b)) joined by a red secant line; the horizontal run is b - a and the vertical rise is f(b) - f(a).

r1-piecewise-1.alt: Graph of the piecewise function equal to x cubed for x < 1 and 3x - 2 for x >= 1, through (-1,-1), (0,0), (1,1) and (3,7); a dotted line at x = 1 marks where the rule changes.

r1-piecewise-2.alt: Graph of the piecewise function equal to x squared for x < 0, 2 at x = 0 and 2x + 1 for x > 0: open circles at (0,0) and (0,1), a closed point at (0,2), and the points (-2,4) and (2,5).

r1-piecewise-3.alt: Graph of the piecewise function equal to x + 3 for -4 <= x < -2 and -2x - 3 for x >= -2: a segment from (-4,-1) up to (-2,1), then a line falling through (0,-3) and (1,-5).

r1-parent-functions.alt: Eight basic graphs with their key points: the constant f(x)=b, f(x)=x^2, f(x)=x, f(x)=|x|, f(x)=x^3, f(x)=sqrt(x), f(x)=cube root of x, and f(x)=1/x with its vertical asymptote x=0 and horizontal asymptote y=0.

r1-transformations-shifts.alt: Four shifted graphs: x^2+3 (vertex at (0,3)), |x+2| (vertex at (-2,0)), (x+1)^3-1 (centred at (-1,-1)), and sqrt(x-2)+3 (starting at (2,3)).

r1-transformations-stretch.alt: Four graphs: 2x^2 through (-1,2), (0,0), (1,2); the reflected cube root -cbrt(x); (1/2)x^3 through (-1,-1/2), (0,0), (1,1/2); and sqrt(-x), which starts at the origin and runs to the left.

r1-transform-abs.alt: Graph of f(x) = -(1/2)|x-3| + 2: an upside-down V with vertex (3,2) through (2,1.5), (4,1.5) and (0,1/2), with arrows showing the shift right 3 units and up 2 units.

r1-transform-cubic.alt: Graph of g(x) = -(1/3)(x+1)^3 - 1: a decreasing cubic centred at (-1,-1), through (-2,-2/3) and (0,-4/3).

r1-transform-reciprocal.alt: Graph of f(x) = 3/(x-2) + 1 with dashed asymptotes x = 2 and y = 1 and the key points (1,-2) and (3,4).

r1-transform-sqrt.alt: Graph of g(x) = 2 sqrt(1-x) + 3: starts at (1,3), passes through (0,5) and rises slowly to the left.

r1-quadratic-roots.alt: Three upward parabolas: one touching the x-axis at a single point (1 real solution), one crossing it twice (2 real solutions), and one lying entirely above it (no real solutions, 2 complex ones).

r2-x-method.alt: Two X-shaped factoring diagrams: for x^2+7x+6 the top is 7, the bottom 6 and the sides 6 and 1; for 3x^2+5x+2 the top is 5, the bottom 6 and the sides 3/3 and 2/3, which give the factors (x+1) and (3x+2).

r2-perfect-square-x.alt: An X diagram with b on top, b/2 on both sides and a times c on the bottom, labelled as giving a perfect square.

r2-parabola-direction.alt: Two parabolas: the one labelled a>0 opens upward and the one labelled a<0 opens downward.

r2-graph-2x2p8xp5.alt: Graph of f(x)=2x^2+8x+5, an upward parabola with vertex (-2,-3), y-intercept (0,5) and x-intercepts near -3.22 and -0.78.

r2-graph-m2x2m4xp2.alt: Graph of g(x)=-2x^2-4x+2, a downward parabola with vertex (-1,4), y-intercept (0,2) and x-intercepts near -2.41 and 0.41.

r2-graph-m4x2m4xm1.alt: Graph of f(x)=-4x^2-4x-1, a narrow downward parabola whose vertex (-1/2,0) touches the x-axis, passing through (0,-1) and (-1,-1).

r2-graph-3x2p2xp5.alt: Graph of g(x)=3x^2+2x+5, an upward parabola with vertex (-1/3,14/3) and y-intercept (0,5) that never meets the x-axis.

r2-ineq-x2px-20.alt: Number line with an upward parabola crossing it at -5 and 4; the rays left of -5 and right of 4 are shaded, with open circles at -5 and 4.

r2-ineq-x2m3xm10.alt: Number line with -2 and 5 marked and the regions labelled F, T, F; an upward parabola dips below the line between them, and the closed interval from -2 to 5 is shaded.

r2-revenue-parabola.alt: Downward parabola of revenue R(x) crossing the x-axis at 0 and 300, with its vertex at (150, 7500).

r2-fence-rectangle.alt: A rectangle whose height is labelled x and whose width is labelled y.

r2-area-parabola.alt: Downward parabola of area A(x)=1500x-x^2 crossing the x-axis at 0 and 1500, with its vertex at (750, 562,500).

r2-power-functions.alt: Four graphs with the points at x=-1, 0, 1 marked: f(x)=x, a line; f(x)=x^2, a parabola; f(x)=x^3, an S-shaped curve with x^5 dashed beside it; and f(x)=x^4, a flat-bottomed U.

r2-power-keypoints.alt: Key points of x^n: for n odd, (-1,-1), (0,0) and (1,1); for n even, (-1,1), (0,0) and (1,1).

r2-power-transformed.alt: Graphs of G(x)=3(x+2)^5-3, which flattens at (-2,-3) and crosses the x-axis at (-1,0), and F(x)=3-(x-2)^4, an upside-down flat-topped U with peak (2,3) through (1,2) and (3,2).

r2-power-sketches.alt: Four quick sketches: f(x)=2x is a line through the origin; f(x)=-x^3 falls from upper left to lower right; f(x)=-3x^2 is a downward parabola; f(x)=7x^4 is a narrow upward U.

r2-mult-touch-cross.alt: Left: two curves that touch the x-axis and turn back (even multiplicity: bounce or touch, never cross). Right: a curve crossing the x-axis at x=2, with a zoomed number line marking 1.9999, 2 and 2.0001 (odd multiplicity: cross).

r2-end-behavior.alt: End behavior: f(x)=3x^5-2x^2+1 falls on the left and rises on the right; g(x)=-5x^4-2x^3+7 falls on both ends.

r2-zeros-graph-a.alt: A cubic-shaped graph rising from the lower left, crossing the x-axis at 0, 1 and 2, and rising to the upper right.

r2-zeros-graph-b.alt: A graph rising on both ends that crosses the x-axis at -4, touches it and turns back at -1, crosses at 3, and passes through (1,-8).

r2-zeros-graph-c.alt: A cubic-shaped graph falling from the upper left, crossing the x-axis at -1, passing through (0,-1), crossing at 1 and 2, and falling to the lower right.

r2-sketch-x2xm3.alt: Graph of f(x)=x^2(x-3): it touches the x-axis at the origin, dips through (1,-2) and (2,-4), and crosses the x-axis at 3.

r2-sketch-m2xp2xm2cubed.alt: Graph of f(x)=-2(x+2)(x-2)^3: it crosses the x-axis at -2, peaks near x=-1, passes through (0,32), flattens as it crosses at 2, and falls on both ends.

r2-sketch-mxp4sqxm1.alt: Graph of h(x)=-(x+4)^2(x-1): it touches the x-axis at -4, rises through (0,16), then crosses the x-axis at 1 and falls.

p1-special-triangles.alt: Two right triangles with hypotenuse 1: a 45-45-90 triangle ABC with right angle at A and legs root 2 over 2, and a 30-60-90 triangle A'B'C' with right angle at A', 60 degrees at B', 30 degrees at C', legs one half and root 3 over 2.

p1-unit-circle-triangle.alt: Unit circle with a point (cos theta, sin theta) at angle theta; a right triangle from the origin has hypotenuse 1, horizontal leg x = cos theta and vertical leg y = sin theta.

p1-radian-circle.alt: Upper half of the unit circle with rays at 30, 45, 60 and 90 degrees labelled pi/6, pi/4, pi/3 and pi/2; the endpoints A and B of the diameter are marked, with arc AB = pi and AB = 2.

p1-sine-graph.alt: Graph of y = sin x from 0 to 2 pi, passing through (0,0), a maximum of 1 at pi/2, (pi,0), a minimum of -1 at 3pi/2, and (2pi,0).

p1-sine-shift.alt: Graph of y = sin(x - pi/2) from -2 pi to 2 pi, with minimum -1 at x = 0 and maxima of 1 at x = -pi and x = pi, drawn over a dashed graph of y = sin x.

p1-angle-addition-triangle.alt: Right triangle ABC with the right angle at B and angle alpha at C; D lies on BC with AD = 1, E is the foot of the perpendicular from D to AC, and angle DAE is beta.

p2-arctan-triangles.alt: Coordinate plane with points (0,1), (0,2), (2,2) and (3,0) joined into three right triangles that meet at (0,1), where their three angles together make a straight angle.

p2-right-triangle-abc.alt: Right triangle ABC with the right angle at B, hypotenuse AC = b = 6, angle 24 degrees at A, angle theta = 66 degrees at C, and legs a = BC and c = AB.

p2-right-triangle-pqr.alt: Right triangle PQR with the right angle at Q, legs PQ = 7 and QR = 24, hypotenuse PR = 25, angle alpha at P and angle beta at R.

p3-param-line.alt: The line traced by x = 2 - 3t, y = 1 + 2t on a grid, with the points for t = -3 through 3 marked and labelled; the line falls from upper left to lower right.

p3-param-circle.alt: The points x = 3 + 2cos t, y = 4 + 2sin t for t = 0, pi/4, ..., 7pi/4 lying on a dashed circle of radius 2 centred at (3, 4).

p3-param-ellipse.alt: The ellipse x = sin(theta), y = 3 - 2cos(theta): centred at (0, 3), one unit wide on each side and two units tall on each side, from y = 1 at theta = 0 up to y = 5 at theta = pi.

p3-hyperbola.alt: The hyperbola x^2 - 3y^2 = 1 in red, opening left and right with vertices at plus and minus 1, and the hyperbola 3y^2 - x^2 = 1 in blue, opening up and down, sharing the dashed asymptotes y = plus or minus x over root 3.

p3-cycloid.alt: A wheel of radius 1 rolling right along the ground; the yellow spot, which started at the paint dot on the ground, has traced a blue cycloid arch, the wheel has turned through angle theta, and a red segment joins the paint dot to the spot.

p3-ex-circle.alt: On a grid, the circle of radius 3 centred at the origin traced by x = 3cos 2t, y = -3sin 2t.

p3-ex-ellipse.alt: The tall thin ellipse x = -3 + cos(theta), y = 2 + 5sin(theta), centred at (-3, 2), of width 2, reaching from y = -3 to y = 7.

p3-ex-parabola.alt: The arc of the parabola y = 1 + x^2/16 for x from -4 to 4, from (-4, 2) down to (0, 1) and back up to (4, 2).

p3-ex-circle-2.alt: The circle of radius 2 centred at (2, 0), passing through (2, 2), with an open dot at the origin, which the curve x = 4/(1 + t^2), y = 4t/(1 + t^2) never reaches.

p3-polar-coords.alt: A point (r, theta) in polar coordinates: a segment of length r from the origin, making angle theta with the positive x-axis.

p3-polar-5-11.alt: In the polar plane, the circle r = 5 and, in red, the whole line through the origin at angle 20 degrees; dashed rays mark 30, 45 and 60 degrees.

p3-polar-5-12.alt: The circle r = 6 sin(theta), of radius 3 centred at (0, 3), with the plotted points (3, 30 degrees), (3 root 3, 60 degrees), (6, 90 degrees), (3 root 3, 120 degrees), (3, 150 degrees) and the origin.

p3-ellipse-axes.alt: An ellipse x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1 with a > b, with the points (plus or minus a, 0) and (0, plus or minus b) marked; the semi-major axis a and the semi-minor axis b are drawn as segments from the centre.

p3-ellipse-vertical.alt: The ellipse x^2/9 + y^2/25 = 1 through (plus or minus 3, 0) and (0, plus or minus 5): its vertical major axis has length 10 and its horizontal minor axis has length 6.

p3-ellipse-foci.alt: An ellipse with foci f1 and f2 on the major axis. A point P on the ellipse is joined to both foci by segments d1 and d2. The top point of the ellipse is joined to f1, giving a right triangle with legs b and q and hypotenuse a. Equal gaps m and n separate each focus from the nearer end of the ellipse.

p3-complex-6-9.alt: In the complex plane, the points w = 2 + 3i, its conjugate 2 - 3i, and -w = -2 - 3i.

s3-synthetic-division.alt: Synthetic division of x^3 + 7x^2 - x + 11 by x - 5: the leading 1 is brought down, each bottom-row entry is multiplied by 5 and written under the next coefficient, and the columns are added, giving 1, 12, 59 with remainder 306.

s5-ex-7-4-2-sketch.alt: Sketch of the graph of a polynomial f rising from f(0) = -3 below the x-axis, through a root at x = 1/3, up to f(1) = 34.

s5-ex-7-5-1-graph.alt: Graph of the cubic f(x) = 0.2(x-3)(x+2)(x+3), crossing the x-axis at -3, -2 and 3, with f(0) = -3.6 and f(1) = -4.8 marked.

s6-root-correspondence.alt: Two mapping diagrams from Problem 7.29: on top, the distinct linear factors of g are each sent by f to a matching factor of f and the map h is labelled bijective; below, g has a repeated factor (x minus r1) squared whose two copies are both sent to the single factor (x minus r1) of f.

s8-box-diagonal.alt: A rectangular box with edges r, s and t; a dashed blue face diagonal b runs across the s-by-t bottom face, and a red space diagonal d runs from a bottom corner to the opposite top corner.

s8-quartic-lines.alt: Sketch of a W-shaped quartic-type curve crossed by two straight lines, each line meeting the curve in four marked points.
